html:
Heightened tensions between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz dominate the global agenda. President Trump rejects a truce offer but anticipates renewed talks, while Iran claims further seizures of US underwater drones. This standoff is coupled with a foiled terror plot near a UK air base used by US forces targeting Iran, hinting at a wider security challenge.

US-Iran Tensions: President Trump rejected Iran's proposed seven-day truce and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, yet expects negotiations to resume next week. Iran insists on "real diplomacy" but warns of "apocalyptic war" if attacked, as its IRGC claims a second US underwater drone seizure. Five individuals were arrested near a UK air base used by the US for attacks on Iran, suspected of preparing a terrorist act; one GOP representative suggested Iranian involvement.

Global Diplomacy: Donald Trump hosted Xi Jinping, reportedly offering to sell US weapons to China, though contentious issues like Taiwan were discussed privately. The US military also prepares to formally end its two-decade-long presence in Iraq this week. In Eastern Europe, Russian attacks killed eight across Ukraine; German and Russian top diplomats held first talks since 2022.

European Politics: France’s far-right National Rally achieved an "historic victory" in Senate elections, securing enough seats with allies to form a parliamentary group. In Serbia, Aleksandar Vučić resigned as president amidst corruption protests, planning to run for prime minister. Tensions flared in Northern Ireland as hundreds blocked a loyalist march in Portadown.

Middle East: Gaza faces the world's worst economic crisis after an Israeli strike killed a Palestinian child and her father. Israel imposed a week-long West Bank closure amid settler incursions into Al-Aqsa Mosque and revoked Dutch diplomats' credentials over banned settlement goods. Details emerged on the 2024 killing of Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah and Egyptian warnings to Netanyahu before October 7, 2023. Regional instability continued as Jordan and Morocco condemned Houthi missile attacks on Saudi Arabia.

Global Security & Economy: Economic forecasts point to "near universal expectation" of global interest rate hikes, with Australia's central bank expected to raise its cash rate to its highest level since 2011. North Korea escalated security concerns by testing swarm attacks mixing drones and missiles. Pakistan saw a suicide attack kill at least 11, claimed by the Pakistani Taliban. South Africa is also reeling from mass shootings that killed 38 people in a week.
